question.text: Two satellites, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>, have masses <math><mi>m</mi></math> and <math><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></math> respectively. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is in a circular orbit of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> is in a circular orbit of radius <math><mn>2</mn><mi>R</mi></math> around the earth. The ratio of their kinetic energies, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></msub><msub><mi>K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></msub></mfrac></math> is:

solution.text:
Let v be the orbital velocity of the satellite which is given as v=GMr

Here M be the mass of the earth, m be the mass of satellite and r is the orbit radius.

Kinetic energy, K=12mv2=12mGMr2=GMm2r∝mr

Ratio, KAKB=mAmB×rBrA=m2m×2RR=1
